reason: The named individual characters appearing in this Exodus 14 passage are Pharaoh (pharaoh of Egypt), Moses (the prophet and leader), and the Angel of God—none of whom qualify as regular people. Pharaoh is a ruler and figure of authority; Moses is a prophet and leader of the Israelites; and the Angel of God is a supernatural being. While the text references groups such as 'the people of Israel' (בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) and the Egyptians, these are collective references rather than named individual characters. No ordinary, unnamed individuals without special status or divine role are introduced by name.
